title: Combinator Primitives: seq, alt, many, and pmap
description: Combine atomic parsers into compound parsers using sequence, ordered choice, repetition, and result mapping.

steps.description: After defining the atomic helpers, implement seq(*parsers) to run each parser left to right, threading the updated pos from one parser to the next and returning (results, pos).
Define alt(*parsers) to return the first parser that succeeds at pos, many(p) to match zero or more repetitions, and many1(p) to require at least one match.
Define pmap(p, fn) to apply fn to the parsed value while preserving the new position out[1], then build between(left, p, right) and skip(p) on top of pmap.

steps.question: What does many1(digit)('123abc', 0) produce before pmap turns it into an integer?
steps.answer: many1(digit) collects each matched digit character into a list and stops at 'a', returning (['1', '2', '3'], 3), which pmap's lambda joins and converts to (123, 3).

steps.description: Combine many1, pmap, alt, and token(p) to parse integers, words, alternatives, and trailing whitespace.
Watch pmap transform the list ['1', '2', '3'] at position 3 into the integer result (123, 3).
